findings.title: Unsafe access of mainHostDestinationCalendar when destinationCalendar array is empty
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` can yield `undefined` when the array is empty, yet the next line does `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` without an optional chain, which will throw a TypeError if destinationCalendar is an empty array (a valid state introduced by this PR). This will crash event creation for any booking where no destination calendar resolves.

findings.title: Mutating evt.destinationCalendar via push creates possible undefined access and side effects on shared array
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is only guarded by optional chaining on `destinationCalendar` but when it's `null` (the fallback branch sets it to `null`), the push silently no-ops instead of including team members' calendars, defeating the purpose of this PR (multi-host destinationCalendar support) for the common case where neither eventType nor organizer has a destinationCalendar set but team hosts do with COLLECTIVE scheduling.

findings.title: Booking.destinationCalendar relation only connects first calendar, losing multi-host information
findings.body: When persisting the booking, `destinationCalendar: { connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id } }` only connects the first calendar in the array to the Booking model (which still has a single destinationCalendar relation). For collective events with multiple hosts' destination calendars, only the first host's calendar reference is persisted on the booking record, so later reads of booking.destinationCalendar (e.g. in handleCancelBooking) will not reflect all hosts' calendars, breaking cancellation/reschedule for non-first hosts.

findings.title: N+1 credential fetch inside loop over destinationCalendar entries
findings.body: `createAllCalendarEvents` and `updateAllCalendarEvents` now loop over all destination calendars/calendar references and, for every entry whose credential isn't already cached, issue a separate `prisma.credential.findUnique` call. For events with many hosts this results in multiple sequential DB round-trips per event creation/update instead of a single batched query, which could meaningfully slow down booking creation for larger collective/round-robin events.

findings.title: Inconsistent destinationCalendar assertions across webhook e2e tests
findings.body: The BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED tests still assert `destinationCalendar: null` while BOOKING_REJECTED was updated to `destinationCalendar: []`. Since destinationCalendar is now always an array (or null when truly undefined per handleNewBooking), these inconsistent expectations suggest the other two test blocks were not updated to match the new array-based contract, risking either silent pass due to loose matchObject or future breakage once the underlying code is fully normalized.

findings.title: loadUsers no longer selects organization.slug, used downstream
findings.body: The rewritten loadUsers() for the eventTypeId path (hosts/eventType.users branch) drops the `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` field that was previously fetched for all users in the non-dynamic case. If any downstream code (e.g. booking links, redirect logic) relies on `user.organization.slug` for users loaded via the eventType.hosts/users path, it will now be undefined, since that field is only fetched in the dynamicUserList branch now.
